# Reading the layout back from text

**Corpus:** 210 synthetic documents, 210 pages, the same records as the headline tables. Rules only, no model. Track: native text, so no character is misread and the only difference between rows is the blocks.

| Blocks | Leak rate | Over-redaction | Escalation rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| native, as rendered (the truth) | 2.5% (1.7% to 3.5%), n=1680 | 22.4% (20.9% to 23.9%), n=3780 | 37.3% (35.8% to 38.7%), n=5460 |
| flattened, every paragraph BODY (scans and releases until 2026-10-17) | 2.5% (1.7% to 3.5%), n=1680 | 41.7% (38.5% to 44.7%), n=3780 | 50.6% (48.2% to 53.0%), n=5460 |
| recovered from the text by `recover_blocks` | 2.5% (1.7% to 3.5%), n=1680 | 22.4% (20.9% to 23.9%), n=3780 | 37.3% (35.8% to 38.7%), n=5460 |

**Is each labelled span read into the right kind of block?**

| Native block | Labelled spans | Recovered as the same kind |
|---|---:|---:|
| body | 3605 | 3605 (100.0%) |
| signature | 840 | 840 (100.0%) |
| email_header | 490 | 490 (100.0%) |
| letterhead | 210 | 210 (100.0%) |
| address | 140 | 0 (0.0%) |
| salutation | 70 | 70 (100.0%) |
| attachment_note | 70 | 70 (100.0%) |
| heading | 35 | 0 (0.0%) |

**Promoted into a role-bearing block the renderer did not put it in:** 35 of 5460 labelled spans, of which 0 had to be withheld. That is the direction that can release a name as an official's, so it is counted on its own (heading read as letterhead: 35).

The `address` row is expected to miss: an inside address and a paragraph are the same thing to the rules, so the recovery does not try to tell them apart and reads an address as BODY.

The recovery was written against these six templates and is scored on them, so the recovered row is an upper bound for a layout it has not seen. `results/releases.md` is the unseen-layout check.
